claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; components inside it inherit the package's version.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository and its version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`, which sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit).

Executable-based plugin packages are distributed as pre-built plugin binaries with per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy), and their version is the version embedded in the binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish executable-based packages to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components alongside it.
Using a single monorepo with one giant package for all components is not recommended by Pulumi because every release versions every component the same way, violating semver.
Link targets exist: private-registry concept page, pulumi_package_publish CLI page, packaging-components anchors, publishing-packages guide, packages and components concept pages.
